title: Ocean Swim Effects
hook: What happens if you swim in the ocean?

beats.line: If you inhale seawater, you cough and panic.
beats.idea: Close‑up of arm in salt water; skin looks tighter and dry.

beats.line: Drinking seawater spikes sodium, leading to dehydration and dizziness.
beats.idea: Close‑up of eyes; tears flow and eyes appear red.

beats.line: Cold water hits, your heart races in a shock response.
beats.idea: Chest view; heart icon pulses faster; character shivers.

beats.line: Your eyes water and sting from the salty spray.
beats.idea: Close‑up of bloodstream; sodium ions highlighted; character’s head tilts dizzy.

beats.line: Your skin tightens as salt draws water from cells.
beats.idea: Character gasps; water rushes into lungs; cartoon bubbles appear inside.

description: A quick look at the body’s real reactions when you plunge into salty sea water.

facts.claim: Salt water draws water out of skin cells, making skin feel tight.
facts.source: American Academy of Dermatology, Salt water skin care (aad.org)

facts.claim: Salt in ocean water irritates eyes, causing tearing.
facts.source: Mayo Clinic, Eye irritation from salt water (mayoclinic.org)

facts.claim: Cold water immersion triggers cold shock response, raising heart rate.
facts.source: NIH, Cold water immersion cardiovascular response (nih.gov)

facts.claim: Ingesting seawater can increase blood sodium, leading to light-headedness.
Swallowing seawater can cause water aspiration, filling lungs and causing panic.
facts.source: World Health Organization, Drowning and water aspiration (who.int)

topic: What happens if you swim in the ocean?
